findings.title: Negative (and zero) litres accepted by the past-watering form and API
findings.where: Beds page 'Record past watering' form; POST /api/waterings
findings.steps: On /beds open 'Record past watering', enter litres -5 and save (or POST {"bed_id":1,"watered_on":"2026-11-01","litres":-5}). Also POST litres 0 or 'Water now' body with litres -3.
findings.expected: Refused with a visible reason ('greater than zero') in the form, and a 422 from the server
findings.actual: Client only rejects exactly 0, so -5 is sent; the server's WateringIn.litres only has le=10000, no lower bound, so -5, -1e308 and 0 all return 201 and show as '-5 L', '0 L' on the waterings page and dashboard
findings.evidence: POST litres -5 -> 201 {litres:-5.0}; litres -1e308 -> 201; litres 0 -> 201; the /waterings page renders '-5 L' and '-3 L'

findings.title: Extreme negative litres render as a huge number string that breaks the layout
findings.steps: POST a watering with litres -1e308, open /waterings at 375px width
findings.actual: The Amount cell shows '-100,000,000,000,...,000 L' (over 400 characters, no wrapping), which forces sideways scrolling; negatives also skew the 'in total' sum, which disappears once the total is <= 0

findings.title: NaN litres and out-of-range ids return 500 Internal Server Error
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (plain text, not JSON)
findings.evidence: All four requests returned 'Internal Server Error' with status 500

findings.title: Bad ?bed= query gives raw validation text and no way to recover except Clear filter; no retry on load errors
findings.steps: Open /waterings?bed=abc, or open /waterings or the dashboard while the API is down
findings.expected: Invalid filter ignored or explained clearly; the error state offers a Retry button
findings.actual: Shows 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer'; the select shows a blank option. The waterings error state and the dashboard's 'Recent waterings' error have no retry (the dashboard doesn't even destructure refresh), so the user has to reload
findings.evidence: SSR HTML of /waterings?bed=abc contains an alert with 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer...'; no retry control in the template

findings.title: Beds list failure on the waterings page goes unreported; the filter is silently empty
findings.expected: An error that says the bed list could not be loaded, with a retry
findings.actual: bedsResult.error is ignored and the dropdown shows only 'All beds', as if there were no beds
findings.evidence: waterings.vue only destructures { data: beds } from bedsResult

findings.title: No request timeout or idempotency on watering POST; a hung or retried request can duplicate waterings
findings.where: Beds page Water now / Save watering
findings.steps: Slow API: click Water now on bed A, then on bed B; A finishes and clears wateringBedId while B is still pending, so B's button is enabled again and can be clicked a second time. Requests also have no 10s timeout
findings.expected: One watering per intent; the button stays disabled until its own request finishes; requests time out after 10s with an error
findings.actual: A single shared wateringBedId is cleared by whichever request finishes first, which allows a duplicate submit; $fetch has no timeout, so 'Watering…' can spin forever
findings.evidence: beds.vue recordWatering: finally { wateringBedId.value = null }; useApiClient has no timeout option

findings.title: Server-local date used for 'today' check: users ahead of the server time zone cannot record today's watering
findings.steps: Browser in UTC+13 just after midnight; pick today (allowed by input max=todayIso()) and save
findings.actual: 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' because date.today() is the server's local date
findings.evidence: schemas.py not_in_future uses date.today(); the frontend max uses the browser's local date

findings.title: Very old dates (year 1) accepted
findings.expected: Refused as implausible, or at least shown correctly
findings.evidence: Rendered row '1 Jan 1 North bed 1 L'
